MoneyMatter shows you where your money is and where it goes. Add accounts by hand or sync them from your bank, and it turns your transactions into balances, a dashboard and reports in one base currency. It goes beyond cash: investments, loans, vehicles and private deals are part of your net worth too. Any AI agent can work with your data over MCP. > [!TIP] > [MoneyMatter Cloud](https://moneymatter.app) is the same app, hosted: a 40-day free trial, no card required. Self-hosting is free and every feature is enabled. ## Contents 1. [Features](#features) 2. [Get started](#get-started) 3. [Connect an AI agent](#connect-an-ai-agent) 4. [Documentation](#documentation) 5. [Tech stack](#tech-stack) 6. [Contributing](#contributing) 7. [License](#license) ## Features - **Accounts** in any currency, manual or [synced from your bank](https://docs.moneymatter.app/import/bank-connections/) through Monobank, SimpleFIN, LunchFlow, Enable Banking and Walutomat - **Transactions** with categories, payees, tags, splits, attachments, [transfers and refunds](https://docs.moneymatter.app/transfers-and-refunds/how-transfers-work/), and automation rules for new ones - **Budgets**, subscriptions and bills with reminders, and loans with a payoff projection - **Investments**: portfolios of stocks, ETFs and crypto with daily prices, plus venture deals and [vehicles](https://docs.moneymatter.app/accounts/vehicles/), all counted in your net worth - **Reports**: a customizable [dashboard](https://docs.moneymatter.app/stats/dashboard/), cash flow, money flow, net worth history and a [pivot table](https://docs.moneymatter.app/stats/analytics-reports/) - **Multi-currency** with [automatic exchange rates](https://docs.moneymatter.app/settings/base-currency-and-currencies/) and one base currency for every total - **Import** from [CSV](https://docs.moneymatter.app/import/import-from-csv/), OFX/QFX, [YNAB, Wallet and Microsoft Money](https://docs.moneymatter.app/import/other-import-sources/), or any statement file parsed with AI. Export to JSON, CSV or XLSX, and [back up and restore](https://docs.moneymatter.app/settings/security-and-account/#backup-and-restore) everything - **AI**: bring your own model (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) for categorization and statement parsing, and a remote MCP server for Claude, ChatGPT or any agent - **Sharing**: share an account or budget with someone, or give a household member access to all your accounts - **Security**: sign in with [email, Google, GitHub or passkeys](https://docs.moneymatter.app/settings/security-and-account/), credentials encrypted at rest, and your data exportable or deletable at any time - **Everywhere**: light and dark theme, a layout that works on your phone, and English, Ukrainian, Spanish, Indonesian and Russian ## Get started **Try it.** The **Try demo** button on [moneymatter.app](https://moneymatter.app) opens a ready-made account with sample data. No sign-up required, and it expires after four hours. **Self-host.** The stack pulls published Docker images (amd64; ARM hosts can build from source) and exposes the whole app on one port, so you can put it behind whatever reverse proxy you already run, or use the optional Traefik + Let's Encrypt overlay. ```bash git clone https://github.com/letehaha/moneymatter.git cd moneymatter/self-hosting cp .env.example .env # then fill the REQUIRED section docker compose up -d ``` Open `http://:8080`. The [self-hosting guide](self-hosting/README.md) covers the full setup, reverse-proxy recipes, every environment variable and troubleshooting. **Cloud.** [Sign up](https://moneymatter.app/sign-up) for a 40-day free trial with no card. Paid plans start at $30 a year. See [plans and billing](https://docs.moneymatter.app/settings/plans-and-billing/) for details. You can move between cloud and self-hosted in either direction with a backup export and restore. ## Connect an AI agent MoneyMatter exposes a remote [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server. Add the endpoint to Claude, ChatGPT or any MCP client, pick the access level on the consent screen, and ask questions the UI can't answer: "Which of my subscriptions got more expensive this year?" or "Where can I realistically cut $500 a month?" ``` https://mcp.moneymatter.app/mcp ``` A self-hosted instance serves its own endpoint. See `MCP_BASE_URL` in the [environment reference](self-hosting/docs/environment-reference.md). Connected apps are listed and revocable under **Settings → AI**. ## Documentation - [Help center](https://docs.moneymatter.app): user guides for accounts, transactions, transfers and refunds, stats, imports, bank connections and settings - [Self-hosting guide](self-hosting/README.md) - [Local development setup](docs/application-setup.md) - [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Tech stack Vue 3, Vite, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS on the frontend. Node.js, Express, Sequelize, PostgreSQL and Redis with BullMQ on the backend. better-auth for sign-in, the Vercel AI SDK for model access, and the official MCP SDK for the agent server. The docs site runs on Astro Starlight. Everything ships as Docker images. ## Contributing Bug reports, fixes and features are welcome. Open an issue first for anything non-trivial, then follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the workflow and the one-time CLA. Translations live on [Crowdin](https://crowdin.com/project/moneymatter). Corrections and new languages are welcome there. ## License This project is licensed under the **GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0)**. - ✅ Free to use, study, modify, and self-host - ✅ Free to redistribute under the same license - ✅ Commercial use permitted (sell hosting, support, custom builds, etc.) - 🔄 Modifications must be released under AGPL-3.0 - 🌐 If you run a modified version as a network service, you must publish your modifications See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for full details. # MoneyMatter **Open-source personal finance. Your finances, your server, your rules.** Accounts, budgets, investments, loans and net worth in one place.
Self-host it for free, or use the cloud. [Website](https://moneymatter.app) · [Docs](https://docs.moneymatter.app) · [Self-host](self-hosting/README.md) · [Cloud](https://moneymatter.app/sign-up) · [Roadmap](https://moneymatter.featurebase.app/dashboard/roadmap) · [Changelog](https://github.com/letehaha/moneymatter/releases) [![License: AGPL v3](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-AGPL_v3-blue.svg)](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/agpl-3.0) [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/letehaha/moneymatter/check-source-code.yml?branch=main&label=CI)](https://github.com/letehaha/moneymatter/actions/workflows/check-source-code.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/letehaha/moneymatter)](https://github.com/letehaha/moneymatter/releases) [![Crowdin](https://badges.crowdin.net/moneymatter/localized.svg)](https://crowdin.com/project/moneymatter)
More screenshots

Net worth history
Money flow

Investments
Transactions

Bank connections
Import sources
Every feature is explained, with screenshots, in the [help center](https://docs.moneymatter.app).
MoneyMatter shows you where your money is and where it goes. Add accounts by hand or sync them from your bank, and it turns your transactions into balances, a dashboard and reports in one base currency. It goes beyond cash: investments, loans, vehicles and private deals are part of your net worth too. Any AI agent can work with your data over MCP. > [!TIP] > [MoneyMatter Cloud](https://moneymatter.app) is the same app, hosted: a 40-day free trial, no card required. Self-hosting is free and every feature is enabled. ## Contents 1. [Features](#features) 2. [Get started](#get-started) 3. [Connect an AI agent](#connect-an-ai-agent) 4. [Documentation](#documentation) 5. [Tech stack](#tech-stack) 6. [Contributing](#contributing) 7. [License](#license) ## Features - **Accounts** in any currency, manual or [synced from your bank](https://docs.moneymatter.app/import/bank-connections/) through Monobank, SimpleFIN, LunchFlow, Enable Banking and Walutomat - **Transactions** with categories, payees, tags, splits, attachments, [transfers and refunds](https://docs.moneymatter.app/transfers-and-refunds/how-transfers-work/), and automation rules for new ones - **Budgets**, subscriptions and bills with reminders, and loans with a payoff projection - **Investments**: portfolios of stocks, ETFs and crypto with daily prices, plus venture deals and [vehicles](https://docs.moneymatter.app/accounts/vehicles/), all counted in your net worth - **Reports**: a customizable [dashboard](https://docs.moneymatter.app/stats/dashboard/), cash flow, money flow, net worth history and a [pivot table](https://docs.moneymatter.app/stats/analytics-reports/) - **Multi-currency** with [automatic exchange rates](https://docs.moneymatter.app/settings/base-currency-and-currencies/) and one base currency for every total - **Import** from [CSV](https://docs.moneymatter.app/import/import-from-csv/), OFX/QFX, [YNAB, Wallet and Microsoft Money](https://docs.moneymatter.app/import/other-import-sources/), or any statement file parsed with AI. Export to JSON, CSV or XLSX, and [back up and restore](https://docs.moneymatter.app/settings/security-and-account/#backup-and-restore) everything - **AI**: bring your own model (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) for categorization and statement parsing, and a remote MCP server for Claude, ChatGPT or any agent - **Sharing**: share an account or budget with someone, or give a household member access to all your accounts - **Security**: sign in with [email, Google, GitHub or passkeys](https://docs.moneymatter.app/settings/security-and-account/), credentials encrypted at rest, and your data exportable or deletable at any time - **Everywhere**: light and dark theme, a layout that works on your phone, and English, Ukrainian, Spanish, Indonesian and Russian ## Get started **Try it.** The **Try demo** button on [moneymatter.app](https://moneymatter.app) opens a ready-made account with sample data. No sign-up required, and it expires after four hours. **Self-host.** The stack pulls published Docker images (amd64; ARM hosts can build from source) and exposes the whole app on one port, so you can put it behind whatever reverse proxy you already run, or use the optional Traefik + Let's Encrypt overlay. ```bash git clone https://github.com/letehaha/moneymatter.git cd moneymatter/self-hosting cp .env.example .env # then fill the REQUIRED section docker compose up -d ``` Open `http://:8080`. The [self-hosting guide](self-hosting/README.md) covers the full setup, reverse-proxy recipes, every environment variable and troubleshooting. **Cloud.** [Sign up](https://moneymatter.app/sign-up) for a 40-day free trial with no card. Paid plans start at $30 a year. See [plans and billing](https://docs.moneymatter.app/settings/plans-and-billing/) for details. You can move between cloud and self-hosted in either direction with a backup export and restore. ## Connect an AI agent MoneyMatter exposes a remote [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server. Add the endpoint to Claude, ChatGPT or any MCP client, pick the access level on the consent screen, and ask questions the UI can't answer: "Which of my subscriptions got more expensive this year?" or "Where can I realistically cut $500 a month?" ``` https://mcp.moneymatter.app/mcp ``` A self-hosted instance serves its own endpoint. See `MCP_BASE_URL` in the [environment reference](self-hosting/docs/environment-reference.md). Connected apps are listed and revocable under **Settings → AI**. ## Documentation - [Help center](https://docs.moneymatter.app): user guides for accounts, transactions, transfers and refunds, stats, imports, bank connections and settings - [Self-hosting guide](self-hosting/README.md) - [Local development setup](docs/application-setup.md) - [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Tech stack Vue 3, Vite, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS on the frontend. Node.js, Express, Sequelize, PostgreSQL and Redis with BullMQ on the backend. better-auth for sign-in, the Vercel AI SDK for model access, and the official MCP SDK for the agent server. The docs site runs on Astro Starlight. Everything ships as Docker images. ## Contributing Bug reports, fixes and features are welcome. Open an issue first for anything non-trivial, then follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the workflow and the one-time CLA. Translations live on [Crowdin](https://crowdin.com/project/moneymatter). Corrections and new languages are welcome there. ## License This project is licensed under the **GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0)**. - ✅ Free to use, study, modify, and self-host - ✅ Free to redistribute under the same license - ✅ Commercial use permitted (sell hosting, support, custom builds, etc.) - 🔄 Modifications must be released under AGPL-3.0 - 🌐 If you run a modified version as a network service, you must publish your modifications See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for full details. The project was previously licensed under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; that license still applies to versions of the codebase prior to the AGPL-3.0 relicensing commit.

repository.readme:
[![Latest Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/mochow13/keen-code?style=flat-square&logo=github)](https://github.com/mochow13/keen-code/releases/latest) [![Build Status](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/mochow13/keen-code/go.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/mochow13/keen-code/actions) [![Coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/mochow13/keen-code/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/mochow13/keen-code) [![Go Reference](https://pkg.go.dev/badge/github.com/mochow13/keen-code.svg)](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/mochow13/keen-code) [![Go Version](https://img.shields.io/github/go-mod/go-version/mochow13/keen-code?style=flat-square&logo=go)](https://go.dev/) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/mochow13/keen-code?style=flat-square&logo=opensourceinitiative&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/mochow13/keen-code/blob/main/LICENSE)
**Keen Code** is a terminal-based AI coding agent like Claude Code or Codex CLI. Written in Go, it is simpler, lighter, minimalistic but useful coding agent for typical software engineering tasks. It supports multiple providers, skills, MCPs, subagents with multi-agent orchestration, and more. Keen Code is highly opinionated. It avoids features that are not necessarily needed or useful for a regular software engineer. It tries to avoid unnecessary complexity and attempts to keep the agent harness as simple as possible. From requirements to implementation, Keen Code was engineered using a wide range of coding agents and agentic IDEs. By far, AI coding agents are the most ubiquitous use case in the era of AI agents. One of the goals of the project is to showcase how coding agents can be used to develop coding agents themselves. This is why most prompts and output docs are saved as markdown files in the [`.ai-interactions`](.ai-interactions/) directory. Keen Code is also an experiment to play with the *new way of working* where engineers work with AI agents to develop software. In this setting, engineers are sometimes referred to as "orchestrators".

Born as an experiment, Keen is now a fully functional coding agent designed for real-world software development.

## Table of Contents - [Features](#features) - [Screenshots](#screenshots) - [Development Philosophy](#development-philosophy) - [Development Cycle Example](#development-cycle-example) - [Install Keen Code](#install-keen-code) - [Install with script](#install-with-script) - [Install with npm](#install-with-npm) - [Run Keen](#run-keen) - [Supported Providers](#supported-providers) - [Built-in Tools](#built-in-tools) - [How Keen Handles Context](#how-keen-handles-context) - [Further Reading](#further-reading) ## Features - **Multi-provider** — Anthropic, OpenAI, Codex (via OAuth), Gemini, DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, MiniMax, OpenCode Go, Yolo-Auto, and Amazon Bedrock. Switch with `/model`. More providers will be added in the future. - **10 built-in tools** — `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `glob`, `grep`, `bash`, `web_fetch`, `ask_user`, `delegate_task`, and `call_mcp_tool`. See [docs/mcp-servers.md](docs/mcp-servers.md). - **Skill-driven MCP servers** — Each connected MCP server generates an ordinary skill (`mcp:`) with a tool table and JSON schemas, so tool discovery stays prompt-efficient and detailed schemas load on demand. See [docs/mcp-skills.md](docs/mcp-skills.md). - **Skills system** — User-defined skills discovered from project and home directories (`.agents/skills`, `.keen/skills`, `.claude/skills`), activated as slash commands and managed with `/skills`. Bundled `commit` and `review` utility skills ship out of the box. See [docs/skills-system.md](docs/skills-system.md). - **Subagents** — Define focused profiles as markdown files in `.agents/agents/` (project or home) with their own provider, model, thinking effort, and permissions. The main agent delegates up to 10 bounded tasks in parallel with `delegate_task`. See [docs/subagents.md](docs/subagents.md). - **Persistent memory** — Global (`~/.keen/memory/global/MEMORY.md`) and project (`.keen/MEMORY.md`) markdown files are loaded into the system prompt every session; the agent records to them when you ask it to remember. Manage with `/memory`. See [docs/memory.md](docs/memory.md). - **Thinking mode** — Extended reasoning for complex tasks. Use `/thinking` to change the thinking effort level for the current model. All models that support thinking can be configured. - **Session management** — Persistent sessions with resume capability. - **Context compaction** — Summarize the conversation into a smaller continuation context with `/compact`, or let Keen compact automatically when the context approaches the model's budget. See [docs/compaction.md](docs/compaction.md). - **Configurable tool history** — Lean cross-turn `TurnMemory` summaries by default; use `/tool-history full` to retain full tool outputs for future turns. More information can be found in [docs/turn-memory.md](docs/turn-memory.md). - **Adversarial review and side questions** — Run a separately-configured second model as an adversarial critic of the main agent's work with `/adversary`, and ask quick side questions with `/btw` without touching the main conversation. See [docs/cli-usage.md](docs/cli-usage.md). - **Input queuing** — Prompts and skill activations typed while the agent streams are queued, previewed, and submitted one at a time as turns complete. Clear the queue with `/emptyq`. See [docs/queuing.md](docs/queuing.md). - **Headless mode** — Run a non-interactive turn with `keen run ""`, with `--format json` output, provider/model overrides, `--completion-signal` gating, and `--session` resume. See [docs/cli-usage.md#headless-mode-keen-run](docs/cli-usage.md#headless-mode-keen-run). - **Permission system** — Filesystem access is guard-checked: working-directory paths pass, sensitive paths prompt for approval, and system or `.gitignore` paths are denied. Always-allow tools with `/allow-permission`. See [docs/permission-system.md](docs/permission-system.md). ## Screenshots

Full interface

## How Keen Handles Context Keen takes a deliberately lean approach to cross-turn context. Within a single assistant turn the model has full access to its tool calls and results. By default, later model requests receive a bounded `TurnMemory` summary attached to assistant messages: where retained tools ran, their bounded invocation inputs, status, and non-zero bash exit codes—not their raw outputs. For ideation or work that benefits from revisiting exact earlier results, run `/tool-history full`. Tool outputs from future turns are then retained in the current session's cross-turn model context. Run `/tool-history none` to return to the compact default, or `/tool-history` to inspect the setting. Full history increases prompt size and token cost; it is not persisted when a session is saved. Subsequent turns therefore receive: - prior user and assistant messages - provider-native historical tool-call/result blocks reconstructed from assistant prose and `TurnMemory` - any pending provider-native state from a turn that failed mid-loop, so the model can resume instead of starting over The default tradeoff is intentional: smaller context and a better signal-to-noise ratio, at the cost of occasionally re-reading files or re-running searches when older observations are needed again. Read-only facts and external observations are refreshed when needed rather than treated as durable evidence. `/tool-history full` lets you choose continuity over that default for the remainder of the session. Here's a concrete example — the `read_file` tool from Phase 3: **Spec** — [`prompts/phase-3/prompt-3_read-file-tool.md`](.ai-interactions/prompts/phase-3/prompt-3_read-file-tool.md) Requirements defined upfront: ask permission before reading, respect FileGuard path rules, text files only, 1 MB limit, support relative and absolute paths. **Plan** — [`outputs/phase-3/output-3_read-file-tool.md`](.ai-interactions/outputs/phase-3/output-3_read-file-tool.md) Design doc produced by the agent: how `Guard.CheckPath` maps to the REPL permission prompt, exact struct contracts, permission flow diagram. **Task** — [`prompts/phase-3/prompt-2_phase-3-tasks.md`](.ai-interactions/prompts/phase-3/prompt-2_phase-3-tasks.md) Implementation broken into steps — tool contract, permission bridge, REPL selector, unit tests — each approved before the next began. **Review** — (inline feedback during implementation) The LLM was rejecting `.go` files because MIME detection flagged them as binary. Review caught this; switched to character-based text validation. The fix landed in the same iteration. ## Install Keen Code ### Install with script ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mochow13/keen-code/main/scripts/install.sh | bash ``` The same command above updates the CLI to the latest version. To pin a specific version: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mochow13/keen-code/main/scripts/install.sh | bash -s -- -v v0.16.1 ``` Installs to `/usr/local/bin` if writable, otherwise `$HOME/.local/bin`. ### Install with `npm` Install the CLI globally: ```bash npm install -g keen-code ``` Update the global install: ```bash npm install -g keen-code@latest # or npm update -g keen-code ``` `npm update` without `-g` only updates local project dependencies. Check that the install worked: ```bash keen --version which keen ``` You can also run it without a global install: ```bash npx keen-code --version ``` ## Run Keen Start Keen in your current directory: ```bash keen ``` ## Supported Providers - Anthropic - OpenAI - Codex (ChatGPT OAuth) - Google AI (Gemini) - Moonshot AI (Kimi) - DeepSeek - Z.ai (GLM) - MiniMax - OpenCode Go - Yolo-Auto - Amazon Bedrock > Use `/model` to switch providers. The ChatGPT/Codex option opens a browser-based OpenAI sign-in flow and stores OAuth credentials in `~/.keen/auth.json`. MiniMax uses its Anthropic-compatible API and includes MiniMax M2.7 and M2.5. OpenCode Go uses an API key and includes GLM, Kimi, DeepSeek, MiMo, MiniMax, and Qwen models. Yolo-Auto uses an API key against `https://yolo-auto.com/v1` and ships the `yolo` and `yolo-small` aliases; the catalog for your key is discoverable at `GET /v1/models`. ## Built-in Tools Keen Code aims to support minimal set of useful tools for coding. Currently, these tools are built in: - `read_file` — read a UTF-8 text file with `N:HASH|` line anchors - `glob` — find files by glob patterns - `grep` — search for text patterns in files - `write_file` — create or overwrite files - `edit_file` — hash-anchored multi-op edits (`LINE:HASH` anchors in one `ops` array, applied atomically) - `bash` — run shell commands - `web_fetch` — fetch a URL and return the content as text (HTML converted to Markdown) - `ask_user` — ask the interactive user clarification questions with preselected recommendations - `delegate_task` — delegate up to 10 bounded tasks to named subagents and run them in parallel - `call_mcp_tool` — call a tool on a connected MCP (Model Context Protocol) server ## Further Reading - [TOUR.md](TOUR.md) — the full story of how this project was built - [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) — release history - [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) — what's planned next - [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — how to contribute - [`docs/`](docs/) — architecture, tools, sessions, skills, and more

repository.readme:
Qamar — Autonomous Coding Assistant for the Terminal

Multi-provider agentic software engineering directly in your terminal
Universal model routing · Isolated git worktree agents · 26 production engineering skills · Real-time budget controls

English Documentation | الوثائق باللغة العربية

--- ## Overview **Qamar** is an open-source, terminal-native agentic coding assistant designed for software engineering workflows. Rather than being tied to a single model provider or cloud-hosted interface, Qamar provides a full runtime environment directly in the terminal: - **Model Agnostic & Live Switching:** Connect to any frontier or local model (Claude, GPT, DeepSeek, Kimi, Gemini, Qwen, Ollama, LM Studio). Switch models mid-session (`Alt+M`) while preserving conversation state. - **Defensive Execution & Verifications:** Real-time token budget ledger with strict spending caps, automatic pre-mutation filesystem checkpoints (`/rewind`), anti-thrashing circuit breakers, and post-edit test verification. - **Concurrent Git Worktree Fleets:** Delegate parallel sub-tasks to isolated `git worktree` environments to prevent git index conflicts and dirty state during large refactors. - **26 Bundled Engineering Skills:** Domain-specific procedural knowledge covering distributed backends, mobile architectures, security audits, and AST analysis, paired with persistent session memory. --- ## Comparison & Architectural Fit Different AI engineering tools serve different workflows. Here is a balanced overview of how Qamar compares with leading alternatives: | Capability | Qamar | Claude Code | Aider | Cursor / Windsurf | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Primary Focus** | Terminal-native multi-provider automation & defensive execution | Deep native Claude workflows in the terminal | Git-integrated terminal pair programming | Full GUI IDE experience with inline autocompletion | | **Environment** | Terminal TUI (React Ink) | Terminal CLI | Terminal CLI | Full graphical editor (Electron fork) | | **Model Flexibility** | Multi-provider runtime switch (OpenAI, Claude, DeepSeek, Kimi, Ollama, LM Studio) | Anthropic Claude models | Multi-provider via LiteLLM | Curated cloud models | | **Local / Offline** | First-class local model support (Ollama / LM Studio) | Cloud only | Supported via local proxies | Cloud-first | | **Multi-Agent Tasks** | Isolated `git worktree` background workers | Single-session terminal loop | Single-session terminal loop | Background agent panes | | **Rollback & Safety** | Pre-write content-addressed snapshots (`/rewind`) + circuit breakers | Git commit history | Git branch commits & manual undo | Editor undo history & GUI diffs | | **Skills & Rules** | 26 modular engineering skills + workspace `SKILL.md` | System prompt guidance | Custom prompt files | Rich editor rules (`.cursorrules` / `.windsurfrules`) | | **License** | Open Source (GPL-3.0) | Proprietary | Open Source (Apache-2.0) | Proprietary ($20–$40/mo) | --- ## Key Capabilities ### 1. Multi-Provider Engine Switch across providers without restarting your session: - **Anthropic:** Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude Opus - **OpenAI:** GPT-4o, o3, o3-mini, o1 - **DeepSeek:** DeepSeek V4 Flash, DeepSeek Chat, DeepSeek Reasoner - **Moonshot AI:** Kimi K3, K2.7-code, K2.5 - **Google:** Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 2.0 Flash - **Alibaba DashScope:** Qwen Max, Qwen Plus, Qwen Coder - **ZenMux & Token Harbor:** High-speed frontier gateways with free tier detection - **Local / Self-Hosted:** Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM via dynamic `/provider` gateway ### 2. Automated Circuit Breaker If an autonomous repair attempt fails twice consecutively on the same file, Qamar triggers a circuit break: - Halts repetitive execution loops and prevents unnecessary file churn. - Atomically rolls back affected files to the last known clean checkpoint. - Re-analyzes the root cause and outputs a structured diagnostic report. ### 3. Git Worktree Isolation Multi-file modifications can be executed in isolated worktrees: - Spawns parallel worktrees via `git worktree add`. - Runs test suites independently on each branch prior to merging. - Stashes dirty working directory states and cleans up temporary branches upon completion. ### 5. Background Update Notifier - Checks npm registry asynchronously in the background on launch without delaying terminal startup. - Local cache stored in `~/.agent-cli/update-check.json` (24-hour TTL) prevents redundant network queries. - On process exit, displays an update notification if a newer version is available: ```text ╭─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ │ Update available: 1.0.0 → 1.1.0 │ │ Run npm install -g qamar-cli to upgrade │ ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ ``` --- ## Quickstart & Installation ### Option A: Run Instantly via NPX (Zero Install) ```bash npx qamar-cli ``` ### Option B: Install Globally via NPM ```bash npm install -g qamar-cli qamar ``` ### Option C: Build from Source ```bash # 1. Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/Moo-101/Qamar-cli.git cd Qamar-cli # 2. Install dependencies & compile npm install npm run build # 3. Link globally npm link # 4. Verify installation qamar --version ``` --- ## Configuration (`.env`) Create your `.env` file from the provided example: ```bash cp .env.example .env ``` Add your preferred model API keys: ```env # Primary Providers (Provide at least one) KIMI_API_KEY=sk-... # Moonshot AI (Default) DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-... # DeepSeek V4 / Chat / Reasoner OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... # OpenAI GPT-4o / o1 / o3-mini ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-... # Claude 3.7 Sonnet / Opus GEMINI_API_KEY=AIza... # Google Gemini 3.8 / 2.5 DASHSCOPE_API_KEY=sk-... # Alibaba Qwen # Optional Capabilities BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY=... # For web_search tool ``` --- ## CLI Usage ```bash # 1. Launch interactive TUI session qamar # 2. Start directly with an actionable goal qamar "Fix authentication token expiry in src/auth.ts and verify tests" # 3. Resume the most recent session in current workspace qamar --continue # 4. Launch with a specific model pre-selected qamar --model deepseek-v4-flash:free "Audit this repository for circular dependencies" # 5. Set financial and token ceilings for the session qamar --max-cost 2.50 --max-tokens 500000 # 6. Unattended automation mode (for Docker / CI environments only) qamar --dangerously-skip-permissions "Run typecheck and fix formatting" ``` --- ## Interactive TUI & Keyboard Shortcuts | Shortcut | Action | Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **`Alt+M`** / **`F2`** | **Model Switcher Modal** | Interactive popup to switch models on-the-fly (`↑`/`↓` or `1-9`) without losing context. | | **`Alt+E`** / **`F3`** | **Thought Inspector Modal** | Inspect real-time reasoning and internal chains of thought with scrollable viewport. | | **`Tab`** | **Autocomplete / Accept** | Autocomplete slash commands or accept proactive code suggestions with a single keypress. | | **`Ctrl+O`** / **`Ctrl+G`** | **External Editor** | Compose complex multi-line prompts in your preferred external editor background parallel agents running in isolated Git worktrees. | | **`Ctrl+T`** | **Background Tasks** | View and manage long-running terminal and background processes. | | **`Ctrl+C`** | **Interrupt / Cancel** | Cancel the active LLM generation or clear current draft without exiting the application. | | **`Esc`** | **Dismiss Modal** | Immediately close any open modal or dropdown and return focus to the input box. | --- ## Slash Commands Type these directly inside the interactive terminal prompt: - **`/model [name]`** — Open the live model picker or switch directly (e.g. `/model deepseek-v4`). - **`/cost`** (or **`/budget`**) — Detailed financial audit: token consumption, prompt cache savings, and remaining budget. - **`/rewind`** (or **`/checkpoint`**) — Inspect atomic snapshots and rollback workspace files instantly to any prior turn. - **`/export [filename.md]`** (or **`/report`**, **`/save`**) — Export full session transcript, executed tool steps, and diffs to a clean Markdown document. - **`/provider`** — Manage dynamic OpenAI-compatible endpoints (Ollama, LM Studio, custom gateways). - **`/mcp`** (or **`/mcp ping`**) — Inspect connected Model Context Protocol servers and measure latency. - **`/memory`** — View and manage temporal institutional project memory and architectural decisions. - **`/parallel`** — Spawn independent background sub-agents in isolated Git worktrees. - **`/context`** — Inspect active context window token distribution and top file consumers. - **`/skills`** — Inspect discovered skills, procedural workflows, and learned project invariants. - **`/overnight`** — Activate autonomous overnight engine for deep, long-horizon migrations. - **`/clear`** — Clear screen history without resetting model context memory. - **`/help`** — Open the complete in-terminal command and shortcut manual. --- ## Native Tool Suite Qamar equips agents with a built-in suite of tools that execute locally with zero external network overhead: - **Filesystem & Mutation:** `file_read`, `file_write`, `file_edit`, `multi_edit`, `files_glob`, `search_grep` - **Transactions & Safety:** `atomic_transaction` (atomic multi-file rollback), `checkpointManager` - **Code Intelligence:** `code_structure` (AST dependency graph and exported symbol analysis across 10+ languages) - **Quality Gates:** `post_edit_verification` (automated test suite runner & circular dependency guard) - **Shell & Sandbox:** `bash_run`, `bash_output`, `bash_kill`, `bash_input`, `bash_wait` with OS-level sandboxing - **Web & Research:** `web_fetch`, `web_search` with strict SSRF defense and CIDR loopback protection - **Institutional Memory:** `record_memory`, `recall_memory` (dual-timestamp persistent knowledge) - **Autonomous Fleet & Skills:** `dispatch_agent`, `submit_plan`, `todo_write`, `use_skill`, `capture_skill_learning` ### Specialized Sub-Agent Profiles When delegating complex tasks via `dispatch_agent`, Qamar provisions isolated sub-agents with curated, domain-specific tool and skill registries to eliminate context bloat: - **`frontend-specialist`:** Equipped with design systems, Tailwind, state machines, and accessibility skills. - **`backend-specialist`:** Curated with database architecture, Redis caching, microservices, and RAG pipelines. - **`test-engineer`:** Focuses on test harness generation, regression boundary enforcement, and offscreen headless UI tests. - **`security-auditor`:** Focused on taint analysis, dependency vulnerability triage, and OWASP Top 10 auditing. --- ## Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration Qamar natively implements the **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**, allowing agents to connect directly to external databases, APIs, and developer tools via standard `stdio`, `http`, or `sse` transports. ### Supported MCP Servers | MCP Server | Transport & Type | Capability | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Semgrep Security** | Bundled Local (`stdio`) | Offline AST vulnerability & secrets scanner with OWASP Top 10 rules. | | **Puppeteer Web** | Bundled Local (`stdio`) | Headless browser for automated end-to-end visual QA and responsive rendering verification. | | **GitHub Suite** | Remote (`@modelcontextprotocol/server-github`) | Repository management, automated issue triage, and PR authoring & reviews. | | **Email Bridge** | Bundled Local (`src/mcp/emailMcpServer.ts`) | Background IMAP/SMTP notifications, drafts, and overnight executive email briefings. | | **IDE Bridge Server** | Built-in HTTP (`src/ide/ideLocalMcpServer.ts`) | Exposes Qamar as a local MCP server for IDE and editor integrations. | | **PostgreSQL / MySQL** | Standard (`@modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres`) | Direct SQL schema inspection, query explanation, and transactional testing. | ### Configuration File Locations Configure MCP servers either globally or per-project: 1. **Global (all projects):** `~/.qamar/mcp.json` (or `~/.qamar/settings.json`) 2. **Project-Local (current repository):** `/.agent/mcp.json` ### Example: Connecting GitHub MCP Allow Qamar to inspect pull requests, manage issues, and search remote GitHub repositories using the official GitHub MCP server: ```json { "mcpServers": { "github": { "transport": "stdio", "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"], "env": { "GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN": "ghp_your_personal_access_token_here" } } } } ``` ### Example: Connecting PostgreSQL & Remote SSE Services ```json { "mcpServers": { "postgres": { "transport": "stdio", "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres", "postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/mydb"] }, "enterprise-api": { "transport": "sse", "url": "https://mcp.internal.corp/sse", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer sk-corp-token" } } } } ``` ### Managing MCP in the Interactive TUI Once configured, Qamar automatically discovers and registers all tools at startup: - **`/mcp`** (or **`/mcp list`**) — Display connected servers, transport types, and exposed tools. - **`/mcp ping`** — Measure live round-trip latency to verify server health. ### MCP Security & Sandboxing - **Dynamic Zod Validation:** External tool schemas are sanitized and synthesized on-the-fly (`jsonSchemaToZod.ts`). - **Fingerprinted Approval Store:** Server launch configs are cryptographically fingerprinted in `.qamar/` to prevent silent tampering with arguments or commands (`mcpApprovalStore.ts`). - **Prompt Injection Defense:** External outputs are wrapped and sanitized against prompt spoofing before reaching the reasoning context (`systemNoteGuard.ts`). --- ## System Architecture Qamar follows a unidirectional, decoupled clean architecture free of circular dependencies: ``` src/ ├── index.ts # CLI shebang entry point ├── cli/ # Commander setup, flags, and prompt lifecycle │ ├── cli.ts # Service container wiring │ ├── promptUI.ts # Fallback permission prompts │ └── banner.ts # ASCII greeting & system telemetry ├── core/ # Agent brain & execution orchestrator │ ├── orchestrator.ts # AgentOrchestrator — reactive turn loop & checkpoints │ ├── tokenBudget.ts # TokenBudgetGuard — live ledger & price matrix │ ├── checkpointManager.ts # CheckpointManager — atomic rollback engine │ ├── loopDetector.ts # LoopDetector — anti-churn & circuit breakers │ ├── planDriftMonitor.ts # Plan drift detector & negative constraint shield │ ├── proactiveMonitor.ts # Proactive verification failure detector │ ├── projectMemory.ts # Temporal institutional memory across sessions │ ├── overnightEngine.ts # Autonomous overnight task runner │ ├── systemPrompt.ts # Agent rules & code integrity invariants │ ├── contextManager.ts # Dynamic compaction & specification pinning │ ├── permissionEngine.ts # Granular permission engine (Allow / Deny / Ask) │ └── security/ # Security enforcement layer │ ├── pathGuard.ts # Path traversal defense (blocks ../ attacks) │ ├── secretRedactor.ts # Comprehensive API key & token scrubber │ ├── systemNoteGuard.ts # Nonce-backed prompt injection shield │ └── untrustedContent.ts # Third-party input sanitization ├── tui/ # Interactive terminal UI (React + Ink) │ ├── App.tsx # Root component & modal window manager │ ├── agentBridge.ts # Event-to-state stream bridge │ ├── layout/ # Terminal text layout & display width calculation │ └── components/ # Modals, InputBox, StatusBar, MessageStream ├── providers/ # Multi-provider LLM gateway abstraction ├── tools/ # 22+ production engineering tools └── sandbox/ # Docker container and OS-level execution sandboxes ``` --- ## Security Model & Known Limitations Qamar is engineered with defense-in-depth security principles. To ensure complete architectural transparency, the following invariants and system boundaries should be noted: ### 1. Security Invariants - **Strict Boundary Enforcement:** Every filesystem modification (`file_write`, `file_edit`, `atomic_transaction`) is checked against `assertPathWithinAllowedRoots`. Reading an external path outside the workspace records read-only access and never grants write permissions to its directory. - **Deny Rule Absolute Precedence:** Explicit deny rules configured in permissions (e.g. `bash_run(rm -rf*)`) take absolute precedence. Even when running in automated environments with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, explicit deny rules and hard-denied system directories remain strictly immutable and cannot be bypassed. - **Binary-Safe Checkpointing:** Filesystem snapshots are captured bit-for-bit into content-addressed buffers without UTF-8 string conversions, preventing corruption of binaries, compiled assets, or images upon rollback. ### 2. Known Limitations - **OS-Level Sandbox Availability:** On Linux, the OS sandbox utilizes Bubblewrap (`bwrap`) for network unsharing and filesystem namespace isolation. On Windows, real process and filesystem isolation requires the `container` sandbox level (via Docker/Podman); the Windows OS level only strips proxy environment variables. Use `sandbox.required: true` if strict isolation must fail rather than degrade. - **Background Shell Execution:** Background processes (`bash_run` with `background: true`) are intentionally run in persistent shell managers to support development servers and watch tasks. Because background processes spawn on the host environment, background execution is disabled whenever non-trivial sandboxing (`os` or `container`) is active. - **Model Cost Estimation:** Exact pricing tables and prompt-cache discount curves are maintained for known flagship models. Unknown, custom, or fine-tuned model identifiers fall back to family heuristics with an explicit console warning and are marked as estimated. Custom exact pricing can be passed via provider configuration. - **Checkpoint Scope vs. Shell Mutations:** The `/rewind` engine tracks filesystem writes performed through agent tools. Commands executed via `bash_run` interact directly with the environment; external side-effects (database mutations, network requests, cloud infrastructure changes) cannot be rolled back via `/rewind`. --- ## System Diagnostics (`qamar doctor`) Verify your environment, Git state, credential access, and provider latency before starting a session using the standalone CLI diagnostic tool: ```bash # Run comprehensive environment health check qamar doctor # Run with detailed network latency and endpoint diagnostics qamar doctor --verbose ``` ```text ╭─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ │ Qamar System Diagnostics & Environment Health Check │ ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ ● Runtime & Terminal Environment ✔ Node.js Runtime: v22.7.5 (>= 18.0.0 requirement met) ✔ Operating System: win32 (x64) ✔ Terminal Stream: UTF-8 encoding · ANSI TrueColor supported ● Version Control & Workspace ✔ Git Binary: git version 2.45.2 ✔ Git Repository: C:\Projects\MyApp (branch: main) ● Storage & Persistence ✔ Global Configuration Directory: ~/.agent-cli (read/write access verified) ✔ Settings Persistence: Loaded settings ● Frontier AI Providers & Gateways ✔ Google Gemini: Connected (209ms latency) · Key: GEMINI_API_KEY present ✔ Moonshot AI (Kimi): Connected (310ms latency) · Key: KIMI_API_KEY present ✔ ZenMux Gateway: Connected (468ms latency) · Key: ZENMUX_API_KEY present ✔ OpenRouter: Connected (351ms latency) · Key: OPENROUTER_API_KEY present ✔ Token Harbor: Connected (369ms latency) · Key: TOKENHARBOR_API_KEY present ● Extensibility & Model Context Protocol ✔ Core internal tool arsenal active (Web Search, Fetch, Git, File System, Sub-agents) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ✔ All systems operational (27/27 checks verified green). Qamar is primed and ready with full autonomous capabilities. ``` --- ## Verification & Test Suite Quality is guaranteed through an automated multi-tier test harness: ```bash # Run strict TypeScript compiler verification (Zero errors) npm run typecheck # Run the complete test harness npm test ``` ```text ℹ tests 1030 ℹ suites 179 ℹ pass 1030 ℹ fail 0 ℹ cancelled 0 ℹ skipped 0 ℹ duration_ms ~53000ms ``` Every tool, provider fallback, circuit breaker, and budget gate is verified on every build. --- ## VS Code Extension Qamar includes a companion extension for Visual Studio Code located in [`vscode-extension/`](vscode-extension/): - Launch Qamar sessions inside the VS Code integrated terminal. - Status bar indicator displaying active model and session cost. - Command palette shortcuts for model switching and plan reviews. --- ## Contributing We welcome contributions: 1. name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, master]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, master]

jobs:
  test:
    name: Node ${{ matrix.node-version }} on ${{ matrix.os }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest]
        node-version: [18.x, 20.x, 22.x]

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      - name: Run Test Suite (1001 tests across 174 suites)
        run: npm test

Qamar — Autonomous Coding Assistant for the Terminal

Multi-provider agentic software engineering directly in your terminal
Universal model routing · Isolated git worktree agents · 26 production engineering skills · Real-time budget controls

English Documentation | الوثائق باللغة العربية

--- ## Overview **Qamar** is an open-source, terminal-native agentic coding assistant designed for software engineering workflows. Rather than being tied to a single model provider or cloud-hosted interface, Qamar provides a full runtime environment directly in the terminal: - **Model Agnostic & Live Switching:** Connect to any frontier or local model (Claude, GPT, DeepSeek, Kimi, Gemini, Qwen, Ollama, LM Studio). Switch models mid-session (`Alt+M`) while preserving conversation state. - **Defensive Execution & Verifications:** Real-time token budget ledger with strict spending caps, automatic pre-mutation filesystem checkpoints (`/rewind`), anti-thrashing circuit breakers, and post-edit test verification. - **Concurrent Git Worktree Fleets:** Delegate parallel sub-tasks to isolated `git worktree` environments to prevent git index conflicts and dirty state during large refactors. - **26 Bundled Engineering Skills:** Domain-specific procedural knowledge covering distributed backends, mobile architectures, security audits, and AST analysis, paired with persistent session memory. --- ## Comparison & Architectural Fit Different AI engineering tools serve different workflows. Here is a balanced overview of how Qamar compares with leading alternatives: | Capability | Qamar | Claude Code | Aider | Cursor / Windsurf | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Primary Focus** | Terminal-native multi-provider automation & defensive execution | Deep native Claude workflows in the terminal | Git-integrated terminal pair programming | Full GUI IDE experience with inline autocompletion | | **Environment** | Terminal TUI (React Ink) | Terminal CLI | Terminal CLI | Full graphical editor (Electron fork) | | **Model Flexibility** | Multi-provider runtime switch (OpenAI, Claude, DeepSeek, Kimi, Ollama, LM Studio) | Anthropic Claude models | Multi-provider via LiteLLM | Curated cloud models | | **Local / Offline** | First-class local model support (Ollama / LM Studio) | Cloud only | Supported via local proxies | Cloud-first | | **Multi-Agent Tasks** | Isolated `git worktree` background workers | Single-session terminal loop | Single-session terminal loop | Background agent panes | | **Rollback & Safety** | Pre-write content-addressed snapshots (`/rewind`) + circuit breakers | Git commit history | Git branch commits & manual undo | Editor undo history & GUI diffs | | **Skills & Rules** | 26 modular engineering skills + workspace `SKILL.md` | System prompt guidance | Custom prompt files | Rich editor rules (`.cursorrules` / `.windsurfrules`) | | **License** | Open Source (GPL-3.0) | Proprietary | Open Source (Apache-2.0) | Proprietary ($20–$40/mo) | --- ## Key Capabilities ### 1. Multi-Provider Engine Switch across providers without restarting your session: - **Anthropic:** Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude Opus - **OpenAI:** GPT-4o, o3, o3-mini, o1 - **DeepSeek:** DeepSeek V4 Flash, DeepSeek Chat, DeepSeek Reasoner - **Moonshot AI:** Kimi K3, K2.7-code, K2.5 - **Google:** Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 2.0 Flash - **Alibaba DashScope:** Qwen Max, Qwen Plus, Qwen Coder - **ZenMux & Token Harbor:** High-speed frontier gateways with free tier detection - **Local / Self-Hosted:** Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM via dynamic `/provider` gateway ### 2. Automated Circuit Breaker If an autonomous repair attempt fails twice consecutively on the same file, Qamar triggers a circuit break: - Halts repetitive execution loops and prevents unnecessary file churn. - Atomically rolls back affected files to the last known clean checkpoint. - Re-analyzes the root cause and outputs a structured diagnostic report. ### 3. Real-Time Budget Sentinel & Token Accounting Configurable spend limits and usage tracking: - Real-time ledger tracking input and output tokens while deducting prompt cache discounts. - Warning threshold at 80% budget consumption and hard stop (`budget_exceeded`) at 100%. - When switching models mid-session, marginal costs reset to reflect the new model rate. - Free-tier endpoints display an active `Free` status indicator. ### 4. Git Worktree Isolation Multi-file modifications can be executed in isolated worktrees: - Spawns parallel worktrees via `git worktree add`. - Runs test suites independently on each branch prior to merging. - Stashes dirty working directory states and cleans up temporary branches upon completion. ### 5. Autonomous Task Runner & The Overnight Engine (`/overnight`) Executes long-running, deep-horizon engineering tasks completely unattended with zero-risk architectural invariants (`src/core/overnightEngine.ts`): - **Shadow Git Worktrees**: Executes all nocturnal work in isolated git worktrees (`qamar-overnight-*`), guaranteeing zero modification to your active working branch until explicit developer review. - **DAG Dependency Pipelines (`dependsOn`)**: Sequences tasks in directed acyclic graphs, automatically skipping cascading dependent steps if an upstream task fails. - **Human Approval Interception Queue**: Automatically intercepts irreversible side-effects (e.g. `git push`, external email dispatches, database schema teardowns, financial checkouts) and safely defers them to a prominent approval queue for morning review. - **Interactive Morning Briefing Screen (`/briefing`, `/morning`)**: Dedicated full-screen TUI presentation on session boot displaying completed tasks, cumulative token/USD cost, git diff review, and 1-click worktree merge or discard actions. - **State Journaling & Zero-Loss Recovery (`/overnight --resume`)**: Continuously journals execution progress to disk; power outages or network interruptions can be resumed immediately without re-executing finished tasks. - **Automated HTML Email Briefings**: Optionally dispatches an executive summary directly to `OVERNIGHT_NOTIFY_EMAIL` upon batch completion. - **Pre-Task Checkpoints & Token Ceilings**: Enforces global token budgets and creates atomic SHA-256 pre-mutation snapshots before every file modification. ### 6. Atomic Pre-Mutation Checkpoints (`/rewind`) Automatic filesystem snapshotting before write operations: - Content-addressed SHA-256 deduplicated snapshots created before any tool modifies files. - Instant rollback via `/rewind` or `/rewind ` restores directory trees to previous states. - Operates independently of git commits, keeping version control history clean during trial edits. ### 7. Persistent Project Memory (`/memory`) Stores architectural decisions and repository knowledge across sessions: - Dual-timestamp tracking for event occurrence (`eventTime`) and ingestion (`ingestionTime`). - Automated supersede detection: superseded rules are tracked rather than silently dropped. - Local persistence in `.qamar/memory/` injected into active reasoning context. ### 8. Bundled Engineering Skills (26 Skills) Qamar bundles 26 domain-specific engineering skills in `.agent/skills/`. Each skill defines architectural constraints, diagnostic procedures, and execution invariants: | Domain | Skill Identifier | Core Engineering Invariant & Capability | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **AI & Local Inference** | `ai-inference-rag-engineering` | Local PyTorch, ONNX, llama.cpp, GGUF/AWQ quantization, CUDA OOM elimination, RAG chunking & GBNF grammar decoding. | | **Backend Architecture** | `backend-systems-architecture` | ACID modeling, Redis Mutex, BullMQ/Celery, Token Bucket rate-limiting, horizontal WebSockets, Outbox & Saga patterns. | | **Frontend Engineering** | `frontend-design-grounding` | React/Next.js, state machines, TanStack Virtual grids, Zod forms, design token math, WCAG 2.2 accessibility & Core Web Vitals. | | **Android Development** | `android-app-engineering` | Kotlin MVI/MVVM, StateFlow, Room WAL, Coroutines, edge-to-edge window insets, automated test verification. | | **Android Compose** | `android-ui-compose-craft` | Jetpack Compose 1.7+, Material 3, foldables/tablets, AGSL shaders, Canvas, sub-frame recomposition optimization. | | **Android Persistence** | `android-backend-infrastructure` | SQLite FTS5, Vector Clocks, CRDT conflict resolution, Ktor HTTP/3, Android Keystore AES-256-GCM / StrongBox. | | **Android Packaging** | `android-packaging-distribution` | AAB/APK compilation, Keystore v2/v3/v4 signing, ProGuard/R8 minification, mapping.txt de-obfuscation, ABI splitting. | | **Desktop Engineering (PyQt)** | `pyqt-desktop-engineering` | PyQt6/PySide6, QThread workers, thread-safe signals/slots, high-DPI scaling, QSS theming. | | **Qt Testing** | `pyqt6-testing` / `qt-gui-testing` | Headless `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen` GUI verification, `pump_until` event loops, `qtbot` signal spies, modal mocking. | | **Windows Packaging** | `windows-packaging-distribution` | PyInstaller standalone bundling, DLL dependency tree isolation, Inno Setup/NSIS installer scripting. | | **DevOps & CI/CD** | `devops-docker-cicd` | Multi-stage Dockerfiles, Buildx, hardened Nginx reverse proxy, Docker Compose, GitHub Actions CI/CD workflows. | | **Security Review** | `secure-code-review` | STRIDE threat modeling, OWASP Top 10, source-to-sink taint analysis, SQL/Command injection & SSRF defense. | | **Runtime Security** | `security-review` | Shell command tokenization, path traversal canonicalization, secret scrubbing, prompt injection guards. | | **Dependency Audit** | `dependency-vuln-triage` | CVE/GHSA audit, EPSS/CVSS exploitability scoring, AST reachability call-graph slicing, zero-regression upgrades. | | **Cross-Tier Contracts** | `cross-tier-contract-integration` | Contract-First schema design (Zod, OpenAPI, Protobuf), reverse proxies, exponential backoff with jitter. | | **Code Localization** | `code-localization` | AST symbol tracing, Def-Use chains, taint-flow analysis, SWE-bench root-cause verification before file editing. | | **Repository Graph** | `repo-graph-navigation` | Topological module layering, Clean/Hexagonal architecture boundaries, token-conserving repository mapping. | | **Performance Profiling** | `performance-profiling-craft` | Memory leak detection, heap snapshots, CPU flamegraphs, EXPLAIN ANALYZE tuning, event loop bottleneck elimination. | | **Verification** | `post-edit-verification` | Multi-tier verification pyramid (compiler diagnostics -> targeted unit tests -> regression boundaries). | | **Planning** | `long-task-planning` | Formal DAG milestone decomposition, strictly monotonic `todo_write` state tracking, disk checkpointing. | | **Code Review** | `pr-review` | Severity-ranked review taxonomy, concurrency race condition audits, architectural consistency quality gates. | | **Git Workflow** | `git-workflow` | Atomic commit theory, Conventional Commits 1.0.0 specification, surgical staging, linear history. | | **Briefings** | `executive-email-crafting` | Technical correspondence, pull request release notes, structured stakeholder summaries. | | **Skill Authoring** | `skill-creator` | Procedural skill authoring, trigger engineering, and exporting reusable skills to `.agent/skills/`. | #### On-Demand Activation Skills are indexed by capability description and loaded on-demand via `use_skill` only when relevant to the task, minimizing context token overhead. Executable scripts inside skills are exposed as callable sub-commands. #### Continuous Learning (`capture_skill_learning`) When a non-obvious repository invariant or bug resolution is identified during a session, Qamar appends the pattern to the skill's `## Learnings` section via `capture_skill_learning`. #### Authoring Custom Skills Custom skills can be added at the project or global level using standard `SKILL.md` format: ```text .agent/skills/my-custom-framework/SKILL.md # Project-local ~/.agent-cli/skills/my-team-standards/SKILL.md # Global across all projects ``` ### 9. Background Update Notifier - Checks npm registry asynchronously in the background on launch without delaying terminal startup. - Local cache stored in `~/.agent-cli/update-check.json` (24-hour TTL) prevents redundant network queries. - On process exit, displays an update notification if a newer version is available: ```text ╭─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ │ Update available: 1.0.0 → 1.1.0 │ │ Run npm install -g qamar-cli to upgrade │ ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ ``` --- ## Quickstart & Installation ### Option A: Run Instantly via NPX (Zero Install) ```bash npx qamar-cli ``` ### Option B: Install Globally via NPM ```bash npm install -g qamar-cli qamar ``` ### Option C: Build from Source ```bash # 1. Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/Moo-101/Qamar-cli.git cd Qamar-cli # 2. Install dependencies & compile npm install npm run build # 3. Link globally npm link # 4. Verify installation qamar --version ``` --- ## Configuration (`.env`) Create your `.env` file from the provided example: ```bash cp .env.example .env ``` Add your preferred model API keys: ```env # Primary Providers (Provide at least one) KIMI_API_KEY=sk-... # Moonshot AI (Default) DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-... # DeepSeek V4 / Chat / Reasoner OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... # OpenAI GPT-4o / o1 / o3-mini ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-... # Claude 3.7 Sonnet / Opus GEMINI_API_KEY=AIza... # Google Gemini 3.8 / 2.5 DASHSCOPE_API_KEY=sk-... # Alibaba Qwen # Optional Capabilities BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY=... # For web_search tool ``` --- ## CLI Usage ```bash # 1. Launch interactive TUI session qamar # 2. Start directly with an actionable goal qamar "Fix authentication token expiry in src/auth.ts and verify tests" # 3. Resume the most recent session in current workspace qamar --continue # 4. Launch with a specific model pre-selected qamar --model deepseek-v4-flash:free "Audit this repository for circular dependencies" # 5. Set financial and token ceilings for the session qamar --max-cost 2.50 --max-tokens 500000 # 6. Unattended automation mode (for Docker / CI environments only) qamar --dangerously-skip-permissions "Run typecheck and fix formatting" ``` --- ## Interactive TUI & Keyboard Shortcuts | Shortcut | Action | Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **`Alt+M`** / **`F2`** | **Model Switcher Modal** | Interactive popup to switch models on-the-fly (`↑`/`↓` or `1-9`) without losing context. | | **`Alt+E`** / **`F3`** | **Thought Inspector Modal** | Inspect real-time reasoning and internal chains of thought with scrollable viewport. | | **`Tab`** | **Autocomplete / Accept** | Autocomplete slash commands or accept proactive code suggestions with a single keypress. | | **`Ctrl+O`** / **`Ctrl+G`** | **External Editor** | Compose complex multi-line prompts in your preferred external editor (VS Code, Nano, Notepad). | | **`Ctrl+V`** | **Clipboard Paste** | Paste screenshots, images, or file paths directly for computer vision analysis. | | **`Ctrl+P`** | **Fleet View** | Monitor background parallel agents running in isolated Git worktrees. | | **`Ctrl+T`** | **Background Tasks** | View and manage long-running terminal and background processes. | | **`Ctrl+C`** | **Interrupt / Cancel** | Cancel the active LLM generation or clear current draft without exiting the application. | | **`Esc`** | **Dismiss Modal** | Immediately close any open modal or dropdown and return focus to the input box. | --- ## Slash Commands Type these directly inside the interactive terminal prompt: - **`/model [name]`** — Open the live model picker or switch directly (e.g. `/model deepseek-v4`). - **`/cost`** (or **`/budget`**) — Detailed financial audit: token consumption, prompt cache savings, and remaining budget. - **`/rewind`** (or **`/checkpoint`**) — Inspect atomic snapshots and rollback workspace files instantly to any prior turn. - **`/export [filename.md]`** (or **`/report`**, **`/save`**) — Export full session transcript, executed tool steps, and diffs to a clean Markdown document. - **`/provider`** — Manage dynamic OpenAI-compatible endpoints (Ollama, LM Studio, custom gateways). - **`/mcp`** (or **`/mcp ping`**) — Inspect connected Model Context Protocol servers and measure latency. - **`/memory`** — View and manage temporal institutional project memory and architectural decisions. - **`/parallel`** — Spawn independent background sub-agents in isolated Git worktrees. - **`/context`** — Inspect active context window token distribution and top file consumers. - **`/skills`** — Inspect discovered skills, procedural workflows, and learned project invariants. - **`/overnight`** — Activate autonomous overnight engine for deep, long-horizon migrations. - **`/clear`** — Clear screen history without resetting model context memory. - **`/help`** — Open the complete in-terminal command and shortcut manual. --- ## Native Tool Suite Qamar equips agents with a built-in suite of tools that execute locally with zero external network overhead: - **Filesystem & Mutation:** `file_read`, `file_write`, `file_edit`, `multi_edit`, `files_glob`, `search_grep` - **Transactions & Safety:** `atomic_transaction` (atomic multi-file rollback), `checkpointManager` - **Code Intelligence:** `code_structure` (AST dependency graph and exported symbol analysis across 10+ languages) - **Quality Gates:** `post_edit_verification` (automated test suite runner & circular dependency guard) - **Shell & Sandbox:** `bash_run`, `bash_output`, `bash_kill`, `bash_input`, `bash_wait` with OS-level sandboxing - **Web & Research:** `web_fetch`, `web_search` with strict SSRF defense and CIDR loopback protection - **Institutional Memory:** `record_memory`, `recall_memory` (dual-timestamp persistent knowledge) - **Autonomous Fleet & Skills:** `dispatch_agent`, `submit_plan`, `todo_write`, `use_skill`, `capture_skill_learning` ### Specialized Sub-Agent Profiles When delegating complex tasks via `dispatch_agent`, Qamar provisions isolated sub-agents with curated, domain-specific tool and skill registries to eliminate context bloat: - **`frontend-specialist`:** Equipped with design systems, Tailwind, state machines, and accessibility skills. - **`backend-specialist`:** Curated with database architecture, Redis caching, microservices, and RAG pipelines. - **`test-engineer`:** Focuses on test harness generation, regression boundary enforcement, and offscreen headless UI tests. - **`security-auditor`:** Focused on taint analysis, dependency vulnerability triage, and OWASP Top 10 auditing. --- ## Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration Qamar natively implements the **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**, allowing agents to connect directly to external databases, APIs, and developer tools via standard `stdio`, `http`, or `sse` transports. ### Supported MCP Servers | MCP Server | Transport & Type | Capability | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Semgrep Security** | Bundled Local (`stdio`) | Offline AST vulnerability & secrets scanner with OWASP Top 10 rules. | | **Puppeteer Web** | Bundled Local (`stdio`) | Headless browser for automated end-to-end visual QA and responsive rendering verification. | | **GitHub Suite** | Remote (`@modelcontextprotocol/server-github`) | Repository management, automated issue triage, and PR authoring & reviews. | | **Email Bridge** | Bundled Local (`src/mcp/emailMcpServer.ts`) | Background IMAP/SMTP notifications, drafts, and overnight executive email briefings. | | **IDE Bridge Server** | Built-in HTTP (`src/ide/ideLocalMcpServer.ts`) | Exposes Qamar as a local MCP server for IDE and editor integrations. | | **PostgreSQL / MySQL** | Standard (`@modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres`) | Direct SQL schema inspection, query explanation, and transactional testing. | ### Configuration File Locations Configure MCP servers either globally or per-project: 1. **Global (all projects):** `~/.qamar/mcp.json` (or `~/.qamar/settings.json`) 2. **Project-Local (current repository):** `/.agent/mcp.json` ### Example: Connecting GitHub MCP Allow Qamar to inspect pull requests, manage issues, and search remote GitHub repositories using the official GitHub MCP server: ```json { "mcpServers": { "github": { "transport": "stdio", "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"], "env": { "GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN": "ghp_your_personal_access_token_here" } } } } ``` ### Example: Connecting PostgreSQL & Remote SSE Services ```json { "mcpServers": { "postgres": { "transport": "stdio", "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres", "postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/mydb"] }, "enterprise-api": { "transport": "sse", "url": "https://mcp.internal.corp/sse", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer sk-corp-token" } } } } ``` ### Managing MCP in the Interactive TUI Once configured, Qamar automatically discovers and registers all tools at startup: - **`/mcp`** (or **`/mcp list`**) — Display connected servers, transport types, and exposed tools. - **`/mcp ping`** — Measure live round-trip latency to verify server health. ### MCP Security & Sandboxing - **Dynamic Zod Validation:** External tool schemas are sanitized and synthesized on-the-fly (`jsonSchemaToZod.ts`). - **Fingerprinted Approval Store:** Server launch configs are cryptographically fingerprinted in `.qamar/` to prevent silent tampering with arguments or commands (`mcpApprovalStore.ts`). - **Prompt Injection Defense:** External outputs are wrapped and sanitized against prompt spoofing before reaching the reasoning context (`systemNoteGuard.ts`). --- ## System Architecture Qamar follows a unidirectional, decoupled clean architecture free of circular dependencies: ``` src/ ├── index.ts # CLI shebang entry point ├── cli/ # Commander setup, flags, and prompt lifecycle │ ├── cli.ts # Service container wiring │ ├── promptUI.ts # Fallback permission prompts │ └── banner.ts # ASCII greeting & system telemetry ├── core/ # Agent brain & execution orchestrator │ ├── orchestrator.ts # AgentOrchestrator — reactive turn loop & checkpoints │ ├── tokenBudget.ts # TokenBudgetGuard — live ledger & price matrix │ ├── checkpointManager.ts # CheckpointManager — atomic rollback engine │ ├── loopDetector.ts # LoopDetector — anti-churn & circuit breakers │ ├── planDriftMonitor.ts # Plan drift detector & negative constraint shield │ ├── proactiveMonitor.ts # Proactive verification failure detector │ ├── projectMemory.ts # Temporal institutional memory across sessions │ ├── overnightEngine.ts # Autonomous overnight task runner │ ├── systemPrompt.ts # Agent rules & code integrity invariants │ ├── contextManager.ts # Dynamic compaction & specification pinning │ ├── permissionEngine.ts # Granular permission engine (Allow / Deny / Ask) │ └── security/ # Security enforcement layer │ ├── pathGuard.ts # Path traversal defense (blocks ../ attacks) │ ├── secretRedactor.ts # Comprehensive API key & token scrubber │ ├── systemNoteGuard.ts # Nonce-backed prompt injection shield │ └── untrustedContent.ts # Third-party input sanitization ├── tui/ # Interactive terminal UI (React + Ink) │ ├── App.tsx # Root component & modal window manager │ ├── agentBridge.ts # Event-to-state stream bridge │ ├── layout/ # Terminal text layout & display width calculation │ └── components/ # Modals, InputBox, StatusBar, MessageStream ├── providers/ # Multi-provider LLM gateway abstraction ├── tools/ # 22+ production engineering tools └── sandbox/ # Docker container and OS-level execution sandboxes ``` --- ## Security Model & Known Limitations Qamar is engineered with defense-in-depth security principles. To ensure complete architectural transparency, the following invariants and system boundaries should be noted: ### 1. Security Invariants - **Strict Boundary Enforcement:** Every filesystem modification (`file_write`, `file_edit`, `atomic_transaction`) is checked against `assertPathWithinAllowedRoots`. Reading an external path outside the workspace records read-only access and never grants write permissions to its directory. - **Deny Rule Absolute Precedence:** Explicit deny rules configured in permissions (e.g. `bash_run(rm -rf*)`) take absolute precedence. Even when running in automated environments with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, explicit deny rules and hard-denied system directories remain strictly immutable and cannot be bypassed. - **Binary-Safe Checkpointing:** Filesystem snapshots are captured bit-for-bit into content-addressed buffers without UTF-8 string conversions, preventing corruption of binaries, compiled assets, or images upon rollback. ### 2. Known Limitations - **OS-Level Sandbox Availability:** On Linux, the OS sandbox utilizes Bubblewrap (`bwrap`) for network unsharing and filesystem namespace isolation. On Windows, real process and filesystem isolation requires the `container` sandbox level (via Docker/Podman); the Windows OS level only strips proxy environment variables. Use `sandbox.required: true` if strict isolation must fail rather than degrade. - **Background Shell Execution:** Background processes (`bash_run` with `background: true`) are intentionally run in persistent shell managers to support development servers and watch tasks. Because background processes spawn on the host environment, background execution is disabled whenever non-trivial sandboxing (`os` or `container`) is active. - **Model Cost Estimation:** Exact pricing tables and prompt-cache discount curves are maintained for known flagship models. Unknown, custom, or fine-tuned model identifiers fall back to family heuristics with an explicit console warning and are marked as estimated. Custom exact pricing can be passed via provider configuration. - **Checkpoint Scope vs. Shell Mutations:** The `/rewind` engine tracks filesystem writes performed through agent tools. Commands executed via `bash_run` interact directly with the environment; external side-effects (database mutations, network requests, cloud infrastructure changes) cannot be rolled back via `/rewind`. --- ## System Diagnostics (`qamar doctor`) Verify your environment, Git state, credential access, and provider latency before starting a session using the standalone CLI diagnostic tool: ```bash # Run comprehensive environment health check qamar doctor # Run with detailed network latency and endpoint diagnostics qamar doctor --verbose ``` ```text ╭─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ │ Qamar System Diagnostics & Environment Health Check │ ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ ● Runtime & Terminal Environment ✔ Node.js Runtime: v22.7.5 (>= 18.0.0 requirement met) ✔ Operating System: win32 (x64) ✔ Terminal Stream: UTF-8 encoding · ANSI TrueColor supported ● Version Control & Workspace ✔ Git Binary: git version 2.45.2 ✔ Git Repository: C:\Projects\MyApp (branch: main) ● Storage & Persistence ✔ Global Configuration Directory: ~/.agent-cli (read/write access verified) ✔ Settings Persistence: Loaded settings ● Frontier AI Providers & Gateways ✔ Google Gemini: Connected (209ms latency) · Key: GEMINI_API_KEY present ✔ Moonshot AI (Kimi): Connected (310ms latency) · Key: KIMI_API_KEY present ✔ ZenMux Gateway: Connected (468ms latency) · Key: ZENMUX_API_KEY present ✔ OpenRouter: Connected (351ms latency) · Key: OPENROUTER_API_KEY present ✔ Token Harbor: Connected (369ms latency) · Key: TOKENHARBOR_API_KEY present ● Extensibility & Model Context Protocol ✔ Core internal tool arsenal active (Web Search, Fetch, Git, File System, Sub-agents) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ✔ All systems operational (27/27 checks verified green). Qamar is primed and ready with full autonomous capabilities. ``` --- ## Verification & Test Suite Quality is guaranteed through an automated multi-tier test harness: ```bash # Run strict TypeScript compiler verification (Zero errors) npm run typecheck # Run the complete test harness npm test ``` ```text ℹ tests 1030 ℹ suites 179 ℹ pass 1030 ℹ fail 0 ℹ cancelled 0 ℹ skipped 0 ℹ duration_ms ~53000ms ``` Every tool, provider fallback, circuit breaker, and budget gate is verified on every build. --- ## VS Code Extension Qamar includes a companion extension for Visual Studio Code located in [`vscode-extension/`](vscode-extension/): - Launch Qamar sessions inside the VS Code integrated terminal. - Status bar indicator displaying active model and session cost. - Command palette shortcuts for model switching and plan reviews. --- ## Contributing We welcome contributions: 1. Fork the repository. 2. Create your feature branch (`git checkout -b feat/amazing-feature`). 3. Commit your changes following [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`git commit -m 'feat: add amazing feature'`). 4. Ensure all 1030 tests pass (`npm test`). 5. Push to the branch (`git push origin feat/amazing-feature`). 6. Open a Pull Request. Please see [`docs/CHANGELOG.md`](docs/CHANGELOG.md) for past releases and architectural improvements. --- ## License This project is licensed under the **GNU General Public License v3.0 (GPL-3.0)** — see the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details.

# Kimi Code CLI [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) [![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-online-blue)](https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/)
[Documentation](https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/) · [Issues](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code/issues) · [中文](README.zh-CN.md) ![Demo of using Kimi Code](./docs/media/intro.gif) ## What is Kimi Code CLI Kimi Code CLI is an AI coding agent that runs in your terminal — it can read and edit code, run shell commands, search files, fetch web pages, and choose the next step based on the feedback it receives. It works out of the box with Moonshot AI’s Kimi models and can also be configured to use other compatible providers. ## Install Install with the official script. No Node.js required. - **macOS or Linux**: ```sh curl -fsSL https://code.kimi.com/kimi-code/install.sh | bash ``` - **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell irm https://code.kimi.com/kimi-code/install.ps1 | iex ``` > On Windows, install [Git for Windows](https://gitforwindows.org/) before first launch because Kimi Code CLI uses the bundled Git Bash as its shell environment. If Git Bash is installed in a custom location, set `KIMI_SHELL_PATH` to the absolute path of `bash.exe`.
